notes: Pedestrian and bicycle counts are not available: the delivered CRIS exports have no pedestrian or bicycle field.
run_off_road counts all single-vehicle crashes (CRIS manner of collision 'one motor vehicle'); it is a proxy, not a roadway-departure flag.
head_on = opposite direction, both going straight; left_turn_opposing = opposite direction with a left-turning vehicle (not head-on).
night = dark lighted, dark not lighted or dark unknown lighting; wet = wet or standing water.

sections.crash_profile: From {{window_start}} to {{window_end}}, this signalized intersection saw {{total_3y}} crashes, with {{ka_3y}} fatal or suspected serious injury, {{kabc_3y}} KABCO injury, and {{o_3y}} no apparent injury. Crash types included {{angle_3y}} angle, {{rear_end_3y}} rear-end, {{run_off_road_3y}} run-off-road, and {{left_turn_opposing_3y}} left-turn-opposing. Night crashes totaled {{night_3y}}. Pedestrian and bicycle counts are not available.
sections.why_flagged: Flagged due to elevated model estimate of fatal or serious injury rate ({{fsi_rate}}), presence in the High Injury Network, high traffic exposure ({{aadt}} vehicles/day), and concentration of injury crashes within 250 meters.

countermeasures.rationale: This treatment is supported for angle crashes, which are present at the site. The cited CMF {{cmf:2333}} is a partial crash-type match and requires engineering review for area setting and severity scope.
This treatment is broadly evidenced for all crash types. The cited CMF {{cmf:1410}} is an aggregate match and requires engineering review for severity scope and treatment prerequisites.

sections.benefit_cost: A numerical benefit cannot be computed for these treatments. The CMF evidence audit does not approve a library entry for calculation, and there is no planning-level unit cost or service life available. Severity scopes do not match fatal or serious injury crashes.
sections.next_steps: Conduct engineering review for signal equipment and area setting to confirm applicability of proposed treatments. Verify geometry, traffic volumes, and existing signal hardware. Assess whether crash patterns align with partial crash-type support for signal head upgrades and retroreflective backplates.
